resources.string: Alerts for ineffective insulin delivery, prolonged highs and ketones; minimum insulin for semaglutide
Experimental safety aid. It does not replace ketone testing or medical advice.
Early low-priority notification (ketones 0.6-1.4 mmol/L, or 2 h above the high threshold)
Pause SMB if insulin seems ineffective
If BG stays high despite delivered insulin, stop SMBs to avoid hidden insulin stacking. Change the infusion set and correct by pen/syringe.
Watch level when BG stays above this for 2 hours. 250 mg/dL = 13.9 mmol/L
Warning after 2 hours above this, critical after 4 hours. 300 mg/dL = 16.7 mmol/L
Illness, fever, vomiting: asks for a ketone check. Switch off when recovered.
Ketoacidosis can occur with normal glucose (euglycemic DKA)
I take semaglutide / a GLP-1 agonist
Reduced appetite and insulin need can lead to ketosis; nausea and vomiting can mask DKA symptoms
Never let the loop deliver less than a percentage of your scheduled basal rate, unless glucose is low. Agree the value with your diabetes team.
Follows your basal profile at each time of day, including a profile percentage
At or below this BG, or when the predicted eventual BG is below it, the floor is not applied
Enter your blood ketone measurement (BHB). Choose the unit of your meter.
Please enter a value between 0 and 8 mmol/L (0 and 83 mg/dL).

string.comment: %1$.1f=ketones in mmol/L, %2$.0f=ketones in mg/dL. Example: Ketones: 1.5 mmol/L (16 mg/dL)

resources.string: Normal (below 0.6). Keep monitoring if BG stays high or you feel unwell.
Mildly elevated (0.6-1.4). Drink water, check the infusion set, recheck in 1-2 hours.
High (1.5-2.9). Change the infusion set, inject a correction by pen/syringe according to your plan, hydrate and contact your diabetes team.
Very high (3.0 or more). Risk of DKA. Follow your DKA plan and seek medical help now. Call emergency services if you vomit, have abdominal pain, fast breathing or confusion.
